acceptanceCriteria: Patterns 1-3 yield distinct non-advisory codes (e.g. RB-BLOCK-NEVER-YIELDED, RB-CHANGE-ON-IDENTITY, RB-ASSIGNMENT-IN-PREDICATE) making the example INELIGIBLE, each pinned by a fixture test; the valid forms (helper that yields/block.call, change{ record.reload.attr }, comparison in satisfy) stay clean.
Pattern 4 yields an advisory code only, never INELIGIBLE.

Pattern 1 resolves helpers across files (shared_context / support files included by the spec) using bound blob content only; an unresolvable or ambiguous helper abstains with a named reason instead of flagging.
Requirements recorded in test-source-analysis-v0.md with traceability; focused tests via heavy.sh; dogfood CEM; Closes #1163.
body: GitHub #1163. For RSpec examples a receipt says passed, tests validity passes four vacuous patterns: (1) a block passed to a helper that never yields (defined in a shared context/support file, no yield/&block/block_given?), so every expectation inside is dead; (2) expect{...}.(not_)to change{ record.reload } or change{ model } on identity-compared values, which can never register; (3) satisfy{ |x| x[k] = v } whose block is an assignment and always truthy; (4) not_to raise_error as the only expectation while the title names an outcome (advisory). Cross-file resolution through included shared contexts and support helpers is required; neighbour of #1140.
title: GH #1163: test-validity (Ruby): flag vacuous expectations (block to non-yielding helper, change{} on reloaded record, assignment in satisfy{}, raise_error-only)
